WOODS RUN DIGEST

Wednesday edition

November 18, 2026

MIDWEST — SOUTHERN ILLINOIS / NOVEMBER 17 REPORT

Shawnee links timber output with forest improvement

Shawnee National Forest reports about 7.3 million board feet of timber generated during fiscal 2026, alongside stand improvement on more than 440 acres and invasive-plant treatment on more than 1,400 acres. Its November 17 account describes timber sales as one tool for improving habitat and forest regeneration.

The forest also reports prescribed burning on 13,297 acres. These are forest-wide accomplishments for the year ending September 30, not a new timber offering or a forecast of work available to bidders.

Forest Service: fiscal 2026 accomplishments →

By the Numbers

Latest available observations as of 2026-11-18. Dates and comparison periods vary by series; monthly figures remain unchanged between releases.

IndicatorLatestChange

−3.1%Versus November 9: US$6.13/gal

−1.1% (calculated)Versus week ending November 6: US$449.00/MBF

−0.4%Versus revised September 2026: 285.6

−4.6%Versus revised August 2026: 900,000

Housing starts are annualized estimates, not actual monthly units, and are subject to revision. The hardwood PPI is an index, not a dollar price. Exchange rates are daily averages. MBF means thousand board feet. The September single-family starts monthly change has a published ±10.0-percentage-point 90.0% confidence interval and is not statistically significant. October housing starts are scheduled for release later November 18; September remains the latest available at publication. The January lumber settlement is verified for November 17; the November 10 same-contract settlement could not be independently confirmed. Display rounding follows the approved format. Changes are calculated from unrounded observations, so rounded currency levels may look unchanged even when a small movement occurred.

Investing.com January contract settlement
CME delivery calendar
Madison’s November 13 index
BLS hardwood lumber PPI via FRED
Census U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate
Bank of Canada daily averages

Action Detector

ROCKIES — MONTANA / APPLICATIONS DUE DECEMBER 4

Montana forestry grants reimburse community tree work

Montana’s Urban and Community Forestry Program Development grants accept applications through December 4. Requests range from US$5,000 to US$20,000, with a match requirement. Eligible applicants include local governments, community organizations, nonprofits, higher-education institutions and tribal governments.

The program supports canopy health, species diversity and landscape recovery; eligible costs can include contracted forestry, arboriculture and planning services. Funds reimburse documented expenses after recipients have paid them. Applicants should review the program’s match rules and consult their local state forester.

Montana DNRC: application, eligibility and reimbursement terms →

Under the Radar

NORTH AMERICA — TRUCK EQUIPMENT / LOW-SPEED POSITIONING

Volvo’s remote steering moves the driver outside the cab

Volvo’s VNX vocational truck can be equipped with Remote Steer, letting the driver position it with a handheld controller at up to 5 mph. Volvo included the feature in its October truck unveiling; November 17 reporting explains the dealer-enabled option and its equipment requirements.

The controller is paired to one truck’s identification number, works only within a limited distance, and has an emergency stop. This is driver-controlled positioning for tight jobsites, rather than autonomous hauling. Truck News lists the required steering, transmission, braking and body-builder systems.

Volvo: truck and Remote Steer specifications → · Truck News: November 17 operating details →

Wednesday Podcast Pick

EP 189: Buy, Buy, Buy? The Lumber Market’s Next Big Trade

The Lumber Word

In this October 29 episode, Ashley Boeckholt, Gregg Riley and Matt Beymer debate buying in a falling lumber market, holding cash, inventory commitments and freight. Their disagreement gives buyers and mill sales teams several ways to examine a purchasing decision. It is a dated market discussion, not a current price report or a trading recommendation.

Listen to this episode

Today's Featured Resource

The Northern Logger App

This field-calculator app collects wood-measurement, forestry, road-work, productivity and financial tools in one place. Use its species and volume conversions, sampling calculations and operating-cost tools as convenient references alongside professional judgment.
